[00:00] Sofia Kim: Hey everyone, uh, good morning, good afternoon depending where you are. Welcome to our October all-hands. Sorry we're a little later than usual, we had some exec sync, but appreciate you joining. We'll go through a brief update from leadership and then open for Q&A.

[00:28] Marco Alvarez: Quick shout-out - the infra team shipped the new kernel selector for the runtime last week, so some workloads are already seeing a, uh, 10 to 15% latency improvement on end-to-end p99 in our internal bench. That's, that's with the new kernel heuristics and some batching scheduler tuning.

[00:55] Sofia Kim: Love it. Marco, maybe during the product segment you can show a before/after link, uh, to the dashboard so folks can see the trend.

[01:10] Priya Desai: On the commercial side we closed two new Dedicated deals in EMEA - one mid-market SaaS and one healthcare customer that required private deployment plus SOC2 and some custom KMS integration. So shout-out to Solutions Eng and Security for getting that across the line.

[01:35] Riley Johnson (from chat, read by Sofia): Congrats team!

[01:45] Sofia Kim: A couple of company numbers - ARR is up 28% year-over-year, MRR growth last quarter was in line with plan, churn remains low. Our runway is healthy given the Series C cash, but we are being deliberate on hires this quarter until the new revenue from Dedicated ramps. So yes, there's a partial hiring pause for non-critical roles, details to come from People Ops.

[02:15] Ava Patel: Quick clarification - hiring pause means we will prioritize critical IC roles and mission-critical managers; if your hiring request is in progress please repost to the new queue and we'll triage. People Ops will follow up with a FAQ doc.

[02:40] Marco Alvarez: Back to product - Q4 roadmap highlights: 1) improve p99 latency via kernel selection and KV cache improvements; 2) Redwood Optimize Beta - automated batching suggestions and quantization recommendations; 3) Private deployment GA for on-prem early access customers; 4) Console improvements for traceability and per-route cost breakdowns.

[03:10] Liam Chen: For Optimize Beta we plan a closed beta with 8 customers, mostly on Dedicated, to validate cost-savings heuristics and ensure no quality regressions. We'll link the eval harness and prompt sets.

[03:32] Maya Singh: Quick question - will Optimize change default behavior for hosted API customers or just be opt-in?

[03:40] Liam Chen: Opt-in for now. We learned from earlier rollouts that we need explicit canary controls so we don't surprise customers with transformer quantization changes.

[03:55] Daniel Park: About Private GA - does that include air-gapped on-prem installs or just VPC first?

[04:05] Marco Alvarez: VPC-first for GA, air-gapped will be an add-on with a slightly longer timeline; we have early interest from two regulated customers. Security and legal will coordinate the audit checklist; we'll share the draft.

[04:30] Sofia Kim: Quick product-market note - our differentiation is increasingly in predictable serving economics and observability. Yes, others have models, but we win on the guarantees: canary rollouts, deterministic latencies, and cost controls.

[05:00] Priya Desai: Sales playbook update - for Dedicated deals we're now using a standard SLA template and a checklist for compliance needs. Solutions Eng will attach the new template to the deal workspace.

[05:25] Casey Morgan (SE): We've started including a 30-minute architecture review in the POC to surface networking/KMS needs earlier. That cut back late-stage surprises.

[05:45] Sofia Kim: People & Culture - we've had strong onboarding NPS this quarter, and the new manager training rolled out. For compensation timing, we're doing an off-cycle for star contributors; People Ops will communicate privately.

[06:10] Ava Patel: Also, all-hands pulse survey goes out later today, please give honest feedback especially about cross-team alignment and tooling friction.

[06:30] Sofia Kim: Alright, quick engineering deep-dive from Marco on kernel selection and caching. Marco?

[06:40] Marco Alvarez: Sure. High level - runtime now profiles typical sequence length distribution and picks a kernel variant at runtime, plus we added KV prefetching heuristics to reduce cold-start generation costs. There's still work to do on memory fragmentation with mixed-quant runs. Some of the terminology may be off in the transcript - we use a home-grown profiler called, uh, 'heatmap' internally but might get renamed.

[07:20] Marco Alvarez: We ran a benchmark - internal customers with long context saw up to 18% token-cost reduction when we enabled smarter prefix caching. Important caveat: caching benefits vary by workload distribution, so the Optimize suggestions will try to detect that pattern.

[07:45] Jordan Reyes: Any SLA changes tied to these optimizations?

[07:50] Marco Alvarez: No SLA changes; these are performance improvements on the same service tiers. For Dedicated, we have a separate latency tier plan if customers want hard p99 guarantees.

[08:05] Sofia Kim: Now we'll go to town-hall questions that were submitted. First up: "Are we planning new regions in APAC?" Priya?

[08:15] Priya Desai: Short answer: yes. We're prioritizing EU and APAC regions for Dedicated nodes next quarter. Cloud cost analysis showed demand in Singapore and Tokyo. We will coordinate with partnerships for local compliance.

[08:35] Question (from Slack): "Will pricing change with Optimize?"

[08:40] Priya Desai: Pricing won't change for hosted; Optimize is a tooling layer - we may have premium features for advanced batching in Dedicated. We'll run a pilot before any list-price changes.

[09:00] Sofia Kim: Next question: "Any org changes in infra or reliability?" Marco?

[09:05] Marco Alvarez: We're creating a reliability sub-team inside infrastructure focused on fallbacks and graceful degradation (model variants, region routing). That team will be lead by Daniel Park as of next week.

[09:25] Sofia Kim: Congrats Daniel.

[09:30] Daniel Park: Thanks. We'll be hiring two senior SREs, one network engineer, and one reliability SWE; these are prioritized despite the general hiring pause.

[09:50] Sofia Kim: Alright, lightning round - shout-outs and wins.

[09:55] Riley Johnson: Shout-out to Solutions Eng for the healthcare deal - tough compliance ask, great cross-team work.

[10:10] Maya Singh: Shout-out to Marco and infra for the kernel rollout.

[10:20] Sofia Kim: Ok closing with a reminder: leadership will post the Q4 roadmap doc and deck in the company drive, People Ops to post hiring FAQ and benefits Q&A. We'll follow up with smaller team breakouts after this for any deeper product or security questions.

[10:40] Sofia Kim: Any final questions?

[10:45] Audience (multiple): No, thanks!

[10:50] Sofia Kim: Great. Thanks everyone, appreciate the work. We'll reconvene next month for a leadership update and a mid-quarter pulse.

[10:58] End of recording.
